text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,291.1, up 0.58% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 rose only 0.08%. Advances outnumbered declines (174 vs 316) but the breadth score of 73.6 still signals a “healthy” market. Bank Nifty led the rally, gaining 0.89% to 61,575.9, and the India VIX (volatility index) ticked higher to 15.68, indicating modestly rising fear.  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹4,864.68 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹3,519.05 crore, extending a 13‑day buying streak for FIIs and an 11‑day selling streak for DIIs. The sector map shows PSU banks, capital markets and FMCG in the leading quadrant, while pharma and mid‑cap stocks lag. Options data point to a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.94 for Nifty (slightly bullish) and 1.24 for Bank Nifty (more puts than calls). The “max‑pain” levels sit at 25,200 for Nifty and 59,000 for Bank Nifty, with resistance walls at 26,000 and 62,000 respectively.  

Watch the 25,400 level on Nifty and the 61,500 mark on Bank Nifty for a break of the day’s rally. Key headlines to monitor include RBI’s two‑day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction on Nov 17 and any global cues from Nvidia earnings, which could sway sentiment. Also keep an eye on the USD‑INR at 93.91 and Brent crude at $93.62, as commodity moves often filter into Indian equities.
